figures.finding: Nigeria's public money for producers is a loan, not a grant: under the Central Bank's Creative Industry Financing Initiative a movie production business can borrow up to N30 million (a distribution business up to N500 million) through its own bank, at no more than 9% a year all charges included, repaid over up to ten years.

value.scheme: Creative Industry Financing Initiative (CIFI), CBN with the Bankers' Committee

figures.applies: Nigeria; movie production and distribution businesses applying through a deposit money bank; terms as the CBN published them in 2019 (whether the window is still open on 2026-11-01 was not confirmed).

sources.said: 2.2 You can get a loan of up to: a) N3 million for Software Engineering Student b) N30 million for Movie Production business c) N500 million for Movie Distribution business … 4.1 The maximum interest rate of 9.0% per annum (all charges inclusive) is applicable to all loans. … b) For Movie Production and Distribution, it is a maximum of ten years

figures.finding: Nigeria has no rebate on a film's production spend; instead, since 1 January 2026 the Nigeria Tax Act lists motion picture, video and television production, distribution and exhibition as a priority sector whose companies may earn an economic development tax credit of 5% a year, for 5 years, on qualifying capital expenditure, if they invest at least N5 billion; the sector's listing lapses after 15 years.

value.name: Economic Development Tax Incentive (EDTI)
value.administeredBy: Nigerian Investment Promotion Commission; credit granted by the Nigeria Revenue Service
value.scheme: Economic Development Tax Incentive (Nigeria Tax Act 2025, Part II, ss. 165-186, Tenth Schedule)
value.sector: Motion picture, video and television programme production, distribution and exhibition (S/N 20)

figures.applies: Nigeria, companies in the listed priority sector, from 1 January 2026 (Act gazetted 26 June 2025); NIPC administers applications.

sources.said: 2.1 The EDTI is a tax incentive scheme that grants tax credit on Qualifying Capital Expenditure (QCE) to priority sectors listed in the Tenth Schedule to the NTA, 2025. The incentive provides a 5% tax credit on the QCE value as it relates to the threshold provided in the Tenth Schedule to the NTA.

Official Gazette No. 117 Lagos–– 26th June 2025 Vol. 112 … 165.—(1)The sectors listed in the Tenth Schedule to thisAct are classified as priority sectors for the purposes of economic development tax incentives. … 176.—(1) The economic development tax credit at the rate of 5% per annum for a period of 5 years shall apply to each eligible Qualifying Capital Expenditure … Motion picture, video and television programme production, distribution and exhibition. N5b 15 years

figures.finding: West African cinemas grossed N15.6 billion in 2025 from 2.79 million admissions and 248 new releases on 122 screens' sites; 81 releases were Nollywood films, which took 49.4% of the box office, and 14 of them earned over N100 million, at an average ticket of N5,596.
figures.applies: West Africa (Nigeria's cinemas dominant), calendar 2025; FilmOne Entertainment's scorecard as reported by Voice of Nigeria; how many films earn back their cost is not given.

sources.said: generating a total box office gross of N15.6 billion from theatrical releases across the region. … The figure, compiled by FilmOne Entertainment, represents admission of 2.79 million cinema goers with 248 new releases screened across 122 cinemas in West Africa. … 14 Nollywood films earned above N100 million as the average movie ticket price for the year stood at N5,596. … Nollywood accounted for 49.4 per cent of the total market share … there were 81 Nollywood films, 92 Hollywood releases and 52 Indian titles screened during the year
